plain: World War II lasted from 1939 to 1945. It began on September 1, 1939, when Germany invaded Poland, prompting Britain and France to declare war within days. The United States entered after the attack on Pearl Harbor in December 1941, though it had been supplying allies before that. The war in Europe ended in May 1945 with Germany's surrender (V-E Day), while fighting continued in the Pacific until Japan's surrender in September 1945, following the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki that August. So while the commonly cited dates are 1939-1945, some historians note the conflict had roots stretching back to Japan's invasion of Manchuria in 1931 and its full-scale war with China starting in 1937.

plain: Solar minimum is the period in the roughly 11-year solar cycle when the Sun's magnetic activity is lowest, marked by the fewest sunspots, solar flares, and coronal mass ejections. The cycle alternates between minimum and maximum, driven by the gradual buildup and release of the Sun's magnetic field, which flips polarity roughly every 11 years. During solar minimum, the Sun's ultraviolet output drops slightly and Earth's upper atmosphere cools and contracts, letting satellites in low orbit stay aloft longer due to less atmospheric drag. It's also linked to slightly increased cosmic ray exposure at Earth. We currently track where we are in the cycle by counting sunspots, a practice maintained continuously since the 1700s.

plain: In the U.S., if your drone weighs more than 0.55 pounds, you need to register it with the FAA and mark it with your registration number. Recreational flyers must also pass the free TRUST (The Recreational UAS Safety Test) and carry proof of completion. Know the basic rules: fly below 400 feet, keep within visual line of sight, avoid flying over people or moving vehicles, and stay clear of airports and restricted airspace. Weather matters too; wind, rain, and cold can affect flight stability and battery performance. Beyond regulations, it helps to understand basic flight controls and battery management, since running batteries too low is a common cause of crashes. Starting with a cheaper practice drone before investing in an expensive one is generally smart.

plain: The Netherlands is the official name of the entire country, made up of twelve provinces. Holland refers to just two of those provinces, North Holland and South Holland, which historically were the most economically and politically dominant region, including major cities like Amsterdam, Rotterdam, and The Hague. Over time, 'Holland' became a common shorthand for the whole country, especially internationally, similar to how people sometimes say 'England' when they mean the entire United Kingdom. The Dutch government actually launched a campaign in 2019 to phase out 'Holland' in official international branding, wanting to promote 'The Netherlands' as the more accurate and inclusive name representing all twelve provinces, not just the historically prominent two.

plain: The oldest form of flight technology is generally considered the kite, believed to have originated in China over 2,000 years ago, possibly as early as 500 BC. Early kites were made from silk or bamboo and were used for military signaling, measuring distances, testing wind conditions, and religious ceremonies, well before anyone attempted human flight. If you count gliding devices more broadly, some historians point to even earlier concepts, like Leonardo da Vinci's much later 15th-century sketches, though those came long after kites were already established. True human flight technology took much longer to develop, with hot air balloons (the Montgolfier brothers, 1783) predating powered, heavier-than-air flight by over a century, which the Wright brothers achieved in 1903.

plain: If you forcefully push an empty, sealed bottle underwater, the trapped air gets compressed as water pressure increases with depth, and the bottle will want to float back up forcefully once released, since the trapped air is less dense than water and creates buoyancy. You'll feel resistance the whole way down, similar to pushing a beach ball underwater, because you're fighting that buoyant force directly. If the bottle isn't sealed, water will rush in through the opening, with bubbles escaping as air gets displaced -- the bottle fills partially or fully depending on its orientation. A rigid bottle might also crack at extreme depths if the pressure difference becomes large enough, though that requires far more depth than most situations involve.

plain: Early fall, roughly late August through mid-September, is the best time to reseed a lawn in the northeastern U.S. Soil is still warm from summer, which helps seeds germinate quickly, while cooler air temperatures reduce stress on new, tender grass compared to summer heat. There's also typically more consistent rainfall in fall than in the peak of summer, reducing how much you need to water manually. Weeds are less aggressive competing with new grass in fall than in spring, giving seedlings a better shot at establishing before winter dormancy. Spring (April into May) is a workable second option, but seedlings then have to compete with weeds and face summer heat stress before they're fully established, making fall the more reliable window overall.

plain: AngularJS is the original framework, released by Google in 2010, built with JavaScript and based on the MVC pattern using $scope and two-way data binding through directives. Angular (often called Angular 2+) is a complete rewrite released in 2016, built with TypeScript instead of plain JavaScript, and uses a component-based architecture rather than MVC. Angular is significantly faster, offers better mobile support, and uses a more modular structure that makes large applications easier to maintain and test. The two are not backward-compatible -- code written for AngularJS doesn't run in Angular without substantial rewriting -- which is why they're treated as essentially separate frameworks despite the similar name. Google officially ended long-term support for AngularJS in January 2022, encouraging remaining projects to migrate to Angular or another modern framework.

plain: Dark matter is a form of matter that doesn't emit, absorb, or reflect light, but its gravitational effects are detectable -- it explains why galaxies rotate faster than visible matter alone would allow, and why galaxy clusters bend light more than their visible mass predicts. It's estimated to make up about 27% of the universe's mass-energy content. Dark energy, on the other hand, isn't matter at all -- it's a mysterious property of space itself causing the universe's expansion to accelerate, discovered through supernova observations in the late 1990s. It makes up roughly 68% of the universe, dwarfing dark matter and ordinary visible matter, which accounts for only about 5%. In short: dark matter pulls things together through gravity, while dark energy pushes everything apart at an accelerating rate.

Depending on your interests, you could focus more on historical sites, spiritual experiences, or a mix of different regions. Given the size of the country, it's generally better to pick a smaller number of places and spend more time in each, rather than rushing between too many destinations and spending most of the trip in transit.
weak2: India has a lot to offer first-time visitors, and where you go really depends on what you're most interested in seeing. Some parts of the country are known for historical landmarks, while others are known for a different pace of life or natural scenery. It's a large and varied country, so trying to see everything in one trip usually isn't realistic. Picking a specific region or route ahead of time tends to make for a smoother and more enjoyable trip than trying to cover too much ground, and it leaves more room to slow down and actually enjoy each place rather than just checking it off a list of destinations.
